fatal_errors: The proposed Y2O3 addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which varies Mo content in a Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing CoCrFeNiMox composite.
No cited evidence establishes that Y2O3 catalyzes a lubricious oxide tribolayer or maintains low friction through 800 °C in CoCrFeNi.
The proposed 1-3 wt.% Y2O3 range is unsupported by the cited direct evidence; E3 studied 0.25-0.5 wt.% and reported no significant friction reduction, with properties worsening at 0.5 wt.%.
The baseline incorrectly assumes progressive high-temperature degradation, whereas the target system has its worst wear around 400 °C and substantially improved friction and wear at 600-800 °C.
Critical test boundaries—8 N load, Si3N4 counterbody, sliding speed, distance, radius, and the 200 °C condition—are absent.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general wide-temperature tribology problem and proposes a controlled baseline comparison, but it is neither a reconstruction of the target material strategy nor adequately supported as an alternative. The target relies on Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening together with low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication and high-temperature silver-molybdate/NiO glaze formation. The generated mechanism instead invokes grain-boundary pinning and an unspecified Y2O3-assisted lubricious oxide. E3 provides limited room-temperature wear support for only 0.25 wt.% Y2O3 and explicitly reports no significant coefficient-of-friction benefit; the remaining evidence concerns generic tribo-oxide protection or different HEA systems. The experiment could test the broad claim, but using a 1-3 wt.% range as one treatment and omitting exact contact conditions would make composition effects and comparison with the target regime ambiguous.
